title: "H: Systemic hormonal preparations, excluding sex hormones and insulins"

date: "2026-02-08"

Corticosteroids, thyroid therapy and the pituitary and hypothalamic hormones.
Sex hormones sit in group G and insulins in group A, so what remains is mainly H01 to H03.

On 21 September 1948 at the Mayo Clinic, Charles Slocumb gave a woman crippled by rheumatoid arthritis 100 mg of Kendall's "compound E" (now known as **cortisone**), and within three days she was markedly improved.
Hench, Kendall and Reichstein shared the 1950 Nobel Prize [@mattesonPhilipHenchDiscovery2024].

|  | Description | In plain terms | Example drug |
| ---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **H01** | Pituitary and hypothalamic hormones and analogues | hormones of the brain's master glands | Somatropin (H01AC01) / desmopressin (H01BA02) |
| [**H02**](h02/) | Corticosteroids for systemic use |  | Prednisolone (H02AB06) / dexamethasone (H02AB02) |
| [**H03**](h03/) | Thyroid therapy |  | Levothyroxine sodium (H03AA01) / thiamazole (H03BB02) |
| **H04** | Pancreatic hormones | pancreas hormones; here glucagon only, not insulin | Glucagon (H04AA01) / dasiglucagon (H04AA02) |
| [**H05**](h05/) | Calcium homeostasis | keeping blood calcium and parathyroid hormone balanced | Teriparatide (H05AA02) / cinacalcet (H05BX01) |

: ATC H level 2 codes {#tbl-atc-h-lvl-2 tbl-colwidths="[9, 29, 26, 36]"}

## Modeling notes

**The assay cannot tell drug from hormone.**
Where the agent is the natural hormone, as with thyroxine and hydrocortisone, the model needs an explicit baseline or suppression step rather than a plain PK structure [@waltersack2004; @melin2018].

**Two regimes, two problems.**
Replacement restores physiological concentrations and is judged on a feedback biomarker, thyrotropin [@chaker2017], or for glucocorticoids on clinical assessment with no equivalent marker [@janssendaalen2024].
Pharmacological dosing deliberately overshoots to exploit an effect the hormone does not produce at normal concentrations [@simon2010; @czock2005].

**Typical structure.**
Turnover (indirect response), not direct concentration-effect [@dayneka1993indirect; @lonnebo2007], with a feedback term when the axis itself is modeled [@bindellini2024] (see [PKPD](/docs/modeling/pkpd/)).
Steroid and thyroid effects run through nuclear receptors and gene transcription [@hollenberg1985], so response lags concentration and shows hysteresis [@ramakrishnan2002].
